title: Requests for My Sons
lede: Pray them one at a time, by name. Pick a son, fill in the names, and print the set.

items.title: A Heart That Knows God
items.body: Father, give {{child}} a heart that knows You for himself and not secondhand through me. Let faith be his own possession, tested and kept. And let our ordinary days — the drive, the table, the bedtime — carry more of You than any lesson I could stage.

items.title: Courage
items.body: Lord, make {{child}} brave. Not loud — brave. Let him do the right thing when it costs him the room, and stand when standing is lonely. Teach him the difference between fear that should be obeyed and fear that should be walked through.

items.title: His Friendships
items.body: Father, give {{child}} at least one friend who will tell him the truth. Guard him from the crowd that would make him small to keep him. And let him be that kind of friend to somebody else.

items.title: Purity
items.body: Lord, {{child}} will meet things on a screen that I met too late and handled badly. Give him a clean conscience and a way of escape. Let him not be ashamed to come to me, and let me be the kind of father a son can come to.

items.title: Work
items.body: Father, teach {{child}} to work — to finish what he starts, to do it well when no one is checking, and to find dignity in it. Break laziness in him early and gently, before the world breaks it in him late and hard.

items.title: His Temper
items.body: Lord, give {{child}} a slow fuse. Let him learn to be angry at the right things and quiet at the right time. Where he has inherited my temper, give him the victory I did not have at his age.

items.title: Humility
items.body: Father, keep {{child}} from arrogance and from self-hatred, which are the same disease. Let him carry his gifts without needing to announce them, and take correction without collapsing under it.

items.title: His Future Wife
items.body: Lord, somewhere there may be a young woman who will one day be {{child}}'s wife. Protect her. Shape him now into a man she will be safe with. Let him be worth the wait.

items.title: Truthfulness
items.body: Father, make {{child}} a man whose word is good. Let him tell the truth when a lie is cheaper. And where he has already learned to shade things, uncover it now while it is small.

items.title: His Calling
items.body: Lord, You know what You made {{child}} for. Reveal it in time. Keep me from pressing my unfinished ambitions onto his life, and give me the grace to bless a road I would not have chosen.

items.title: Protection
items.body: Father, guard {{child}} — his body, his mind, his going out and coming in. From what I can see and from what I cannot, cover him.

items.title: That He Would Be Forgiven
items.body: Lord, more than success, more than safety, I ask that {{child}} would be forgiven. Bring him to the cross. Let him know the weight of his sin and the greater weight of Your mercy.
